raw_response:
I’m 40, been farming these 4 mu for 15 years now. Didn’t go past primary school, but I know this land better than any book. My wife works at a garment factory in town and my two kids are in school, so during busy times it’s mostly me in the fields. We need to be careful with money—4 mu isn’t much, and with only my wife’s off-farm wages we just get by. Every yuan I spend on inputs is a yuan I don’t have for the kids’ school fees or emergencies.

**Wheat:** I’ll plant around October 10th, right after the National Day holiday. Last year I was almost a week late and the wheat didn’t tiller well before winter. I’m using the same improved variety as my neighbor Old Wang—his wheat always looks strong. About 15 jin of seed per mu, costs around 18 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I’ll buy two bags of compound fertilizer and spread half a bag per mu at planting. Then when the wheat turns green around Qingming, I’ll topdress with half a bag of urea per mu. That’s about 15 kg of nitrogen if you count it that way—I don’t count it, I just know it’s one bag spread across my plot. I know the extension office says to use more, but my neighbor uses about the same and his wheat does fine. I’ll irrigate three times: right after planting to help it sprout, once before winter freeze, and once at jointing in April. Pumping costs 15 yuan each time per mu, so that’s real money. If it’s very dry at grain filling I might do a fourth, but I’ll wait and see. I’ll spray herbicide once in spring. I’ll do rotary tillage after the maize comes off, then broadcast the seed. Wheat harvest is hard—I’ll need to hire one person for a day, that’s 100 yuan now. I expect about 400 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

**Maize:** The big problem is always the rush after wheat harvest in June. We have maybe five or six days to get the maize in the ground before it gets too late. I’ll hire one person for two days during that craziness—one day to help cut wheat and one day to help plant maize. I use hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu, costs about 28 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer and urea in the planting hole—about half a bag of compound and a bit less than half a bag of urea per mu. I won’t topdress maize unless the leaves turn really yellow; maize is tough and I need to save the money. I’ll irrigate once in July if it doesn’t rain, otherwise I’ll rely on the sky. One herbicide spray when the maize is small. I’ll use minimal tillage—maybe light rotary tillage after wheat, then plant with my small hand planter. Maize is easier than wheat, maybe 8 days of family labor total. I expect around 450 kg per mu.

I thought about buying more fertilizer for both crops, but if I spend too much now and someone gets sick, I won’t have cash in hand. Better to be a little safe. My total spending on seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation, and hired help will be around 1,680 yuan this year.
